items.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021
items.q: I was so busy listening to Trane I was overlooking Cannonball.

ctx.x: You know it takes an open-minded producer I think to just, or at least someone who just stays out of the way.

Monk that’s the whole key. ‘Cause Bob Thiele never got in the way but I guess you know he — Bob Thiele produced all those records by John Coltrane. And then he told me a story about the record he produced with John Coltrane and Duke Ellington. And Bob Thiele, you know, if you let him he’d have you doing two and three takes. So Duke Ellington and Trane, they performed the song so Bob came out and said, “Okay let’s do another take.” Duke Ellington told him, said, “No, it’s going to be different anyway.”

The sound that you got on the Rhodes and carried you through different recordings, were you hearing that, I mean there was a lot of tremolo, some reverb, some effects. I’m trying to think how to ask this question. When you were recording were you hearing those effects or were they added later?
